name: Ingenuity

parts.name: Twin rotors
parts.role: Dual counter-rotating carbon fiber blades spinning at 2,400 RPM

parts.name: Solar panel
parts.role: Small solar array mounted above the rotor mast to recharge Li-ion cells

parts.name: Fuselage
parts.role: Insulated cube housing lithium-ion batteries, computer, and inertial sensors

parts.name: Landing legs
parts.role: Four flexible composite carbon-fiber legs to absorb landing shock
parts.snap: Four composite landing struts in position.

parts.name: Downward camera
parts.role: Black-and-white downward navigation camera tracking surface visual features

parts.name: Antenna
parts.role: Vertical whip antenna communicating with the Perseverance rover

challenge.title: Hover at 3 meters
challenge.intro: Spin up the dual rotors in the razor-thin Martian atmosphere. Throttle the rotor speed to lift off and maintain a steady 3-meter hover for 30 seconds.
challenge.hint: In Mars' 1% atmosphere, rotors need high RPM to bite the air. Keep throttle balanced around the target line.

signal_note: A hard landing in sandy ripple terrain on flight 72 fractured a blade tip, ending its flight career.
ending: Ingenuity proved that powered aerial flight is possible in the thin atmosphere of another world.
